title: Resting-State EEG and Trait Anxiety
description: Resting-state EEG recordings from 51 undergraduate participants at the University of Alberta, collected to examine how resting-state alpha and theta power and oscillatory dynamics relate to trait anxiety. Each participant completed alternating eyes-open and eyes-closed blocks, and the dataset includes preprocessed EEG along with questionnaire scores for anxiety and personality (STAI, TIPI, BIS/FFFS).
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 256-channel EGI HydroCel Geodesic Sensor Net at 500 Hz (online reference Cz). The protocol was four 1-minute blocks (EO-EC-EO-EC) signaled by auditory beeps. Preprocessing in EEGLAB included 0.1-50 Hz bandpass filtering, CleanLine line-noise removal, kurtosis-based channel rejection, average re-referencing, extended runica ICA with ICLabel and visual artifact component removal, and spherical interpolation.
